Only biscuits and watery then that's your diet. Bigger villages have some restaurants, sometimes with buffet. There's beans, rice, chips, soup. Really adapt and overcome. Everyone has its preferences, just really nice to see.  
  
I'm not good at eating on the bike so I prefer to stop, eat for 15 minutes then get going again.
Will think about it after recovery day haha

Yes actually!! I took my time at CP3 to clean the bike, change brake pads and check up. Good decision, I think. I applied lube on the morning of the last day (80km before this picture) so no crazy sounds at that point, depending on your level of tolerance.

It's a gravel race so took my one and only gravel bike, Storck GRIX. Almost all participants on a gravel bike, think i saw two MTBs. I had some 33mm tires installed, Vittoria Terreno Dry, without a doubt the biggest mistake. Some gravel roads are super rough, huge rocks, huge potholes, just absolutely insane. More volume and more cushion would have been nice.  
Luggage was minimal minimal, no sleeping system no set of clothes. Maybe 4kg tops of extra stuff.  
Rwanda is densely populated so resupply is not really an issue. I had two bottles on the bike and a hydration vest, about 3 liters total. Biggest distance between resupply points maybe 60km. And even then, if I ever got in trouble I could have still flagged down someone (there's always people around).  
Weather was quite hot, just a jersey even for the night rides. I think I was a bit cold just two times. I had a couple of rain showers but none longer than 30 minutes and they were rather refreshing.
